title: Quantum Hamiltonian Evolution for Coherent Quantum Learning
authors: Ignacio B. Acedo, Javier Gonzalez-Conde, Pablo Rodriguez-Grasa, Barry C. Sanders, Lirandë Pira
abstract: We introduce Coherent Quantum Learning (CQL), a training framework for quantum learning models in which the model parameters are quantum degrees of freedom evolved under a Hamiltonian that encodes the loss function. Current quantum machine learning retains classical optimization: parameters are updated by a classical outer loop using gradient estimates from measurements, and quantum coherence has no role in the training dynamics, just as in any classical treatment of the same problem. In the quantum case, a parameter register initialized in superposition evolves unitarily, and probability amplitude concentrates near low-loss configurations through interference, without gradient computation or classical feedback. We give an explicit construction using block encodings and Hamiltonian simulation, applicable to arbitrary parameterized circuits. Numerical experiments on binary classification and interferometric phase estimation confirm that the evolved distribution peaks at the optimal parameters, matching gradient-based performance. The construction is compatible in principle with fault-tolerant implementations and extends to batched training via sequential Hamiltonian evolution.
summary: This paper proposes Coherent Quantum Learning (CQL), a novel quantum training framework where the optimization process is replaced by coherent Hamiltonian evolution. By encoding the loss function into the system's Hamiltonian, the system naturally evolves toward parameters that minimize the loss through quantum interference. This offers a purely quantum alternative to classical gradient-based optimization in quantum machine learning.
main_problem: The paper addresses the need for a quantum mechanical training framework for quantum machine learning, moving beyond classical optimization loops.
main_result: It introduces Coherent Quantum Learning (CQL), a framework where parameter evolution is governed by a Hamiltonian encoding the loss function, achieving optimal parameter estimation via quantum interference.
method: The training is realized by evolving the system unitarily under a time-dependent Hamiltonian that combines kinetic terms and a loss-encoding Hamiltonian. This process replaces classical gradient estimation with coherent interference.
model_or_system: The model uses a parameterized quantum circuit whose parameters are treated as quantum degrees of freedom. The loss function $L(x, 	heta)$ is encoded into a diagonal Hamiltonian $\hat{H}_L$ acting on the parameter register.
key_observables: The probability amplitude concentrating near low-loss configurations, and the final state distribution peaking at optimal parameters.
important_parameters: The evolution time $	au$, the structure of the loss Hamiltonian $\hat{H}_L$, and the batch size for sequential updates.
main_assumptions: The framework assumes the ability to construct block encodings for the loss Hamiltonian and relies on sequential evolution for batched training.
figures_summary: Figure 1 conceptually contrasts traditional hybrid training with CQL's loss-guided evolution. Figure 6 numerically compares the loss evolution of CQL against traditional gradient descent for a 1D binary classification task.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the CQL concept, detailing the Hamiltonian construction using block encodings for various loss types (polynomial, smooth). It then details the sequential, batched training algorithm and validates the approach with numerical simulations on classification and phase estimation tasks.
why_interesting: The core idea of encoding optimization into Hamiltonian dynamics is highly relevant to AMO physics, suggesting that physical evolution itself can perform complex computational tasks like optimization, potentially linking quantum simulation to machine learning.

In CQL (right), the model parameters are promoted to quantum degrees of freedom, the objective function is en- coded as a loss Hamiltonian, and training is realized through coherent Hamiltonian evolution.
